name: Brentuximab vedotin

discovery.note: Chimeric anti-CD30 antibody cAC10 linked via a protease-cleavable linker to monomethyl auristatin E.

tagline: CD30-targeted ADC for Hodgkin lymphoma and CD30-positive T-cell lymphomas
summary: Brentuximab vedotin is an antibody–drug conjugate that targets CD30 and delivers the microtubule inhibitor MMAE. It is used in classical Hodgkin lymphoma, systemic anaplastic large cell lymphoma and other CD30-positive lymphomas.
mechanism: The antibody binds CD30 (TNFRSF8), which is highly expressed on Reed–Sternberg cells of Hodgkin lymphoma and on anaplastic large cell lymphoma cells.

After internalisation, the linker is cleaved by lysosomal proteases, releasing MMAE, which disrupts the microtubule network, arrests the cell cycle and triggers apoptosis; free MMAE can also kill adjacent cells.
uses: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma (frontline with AVD, relapsed, post-transplant consolidation)
Primary cutaneous ALCL and CD30-expressing mycosis fungoides
Relapsed large B-cell lymphoma (with lenalidomide and rituximab)

history.title: Takeda partnership
history.detail: Millennium (Takeda) gains ex-US rights to brentuximab vedotin.

history.title: FDA accelerated approval
history.detail: Approved in August for relapsed Hodgkin lymphoma and systemic ALCL.

history.title: EU approval
history.detail: Conditional approval in the European Union.

history.title: PML boxed warning
history.detail: FDA adds a boxed warning for progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy.

history.title: Frontline approvals
history.detail: Approved with AVD for stage III–IV Hodgkin lymphoma (ECHELON-1) and with CHP for CD30-positive PTCL (ECHELON-2).

history.title: Pfizer acquires Seagen
history.detail: US rights pass to Pfizer with the Seagen acquisition.

history.title: Large B-cell lymphoma
history.detail: FDA approves it with lenalidomide and rituximab for relapsed large B-cell lymphoma (ECHELON-3).

pk.metabolism: Antibody catabolised; MMAE metabolised by CYP3A4

facts: Combination with bleomycin is contraindicated because of pulmonary toxicity.
CD30 was first identified as a marker of Reed–Sternberg cells in Hodgkin lymphoma.
